attributes.title: Level 6

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓Did you add the Scroller extension to the editor?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How was the Background Scroll extension used in the blocks editor?

❓ What might the Background Scroll extension be used for in this project?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Make sure the ninja has selected the arcade-background-scroll extension to the project and the Scroller menu is available in the editor.

💡 Remind the ninja of how they used the Background Scroll extension in the blocks editor. This extension enables the background to move in different directions on screen, matching the movement of sprites. In this project, the parallax feature will be used, enabling different background layers to move at different speeds.
steps.instructions:
Add the Background Scroll extension to create a project with scrolling background layers!


Add the Background Scroll extension by clicking More then selecting Extensions. Scroll down then select the arcade-background-scroll extension to add it to the project.


Now, Scroller will appear on the code menu and the code blocks inside it can be used in the project.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you set the layer parameters to different values in the setLayerImage functions?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓How is the setLayerImage function different than the setBackgroundImage function?

❓ What background image is displayed when the project runs?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡The setLayerImage and setBackgroundImage functions both display a background image on screen. The setLayerImage function takes this a step further and creates different layers of the background image that can be stacked on top of each other.

💡 Explain to the ninja that the setLayerImage function works similarly to the z-position, or depth level of a sprite. The function assigns a layer number to a background image. The higher the number, the closer that layer is to the camera, making it appear in front of the layers with lower numbers. In this example, because the sky image is layer 0 and the clouds image is layer 1, the clouds will appear in front of the sky.
steps.instructions:
Create a background of multiple layers!


Open Scroller and drag [set image for (layer) to (image)] underneath // scrolling background set up. Notice how the code block turns into JavaScript text:

scroller.setLayerImage(scroller.

BackgroundLayer, img` `)


The setLayerImage function takes 2 parameters: layer and image. Update the layer parameter by typing a dot operator after BackgroundLayer. Select Layer0 from the code completion tool, then update the image parameter so that the sky image variable is set to Layer0 of the background.


Open Scroller and drag another [set image for (layer) to (image)] under the existing code. Update the layer and image parameters so that the clouds image variable is set to Layer1 of the background.


Click ▶ to see the cloud image appear in front of the sky image on screen!

steps.hints: ❓Did you use a comma to add the layer parameter to the scrollBackgroundWithSpeed function, then update the layer parameter with 2 dot operators?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What does the scrollBackgroundWithSpeed function do? How is it being used in this project?

❓ What background image will scroll when the scrollBackgroundWithSpeed code runs?

❓ What values will cause the background layer to scroll left? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 The scrollBackgroundWithSpeed function enables an individual background layer to scroll across the screen. The parameters allow the coder to determine the direction, speed, and layer that will scroll on the screen. In this example, the clouds image at layer 1 will scroll horizontally left on screen.

💡 Remind the ninja that a positive vx value will cause the background layer to move right and a negative vx value will cause it to move left. A positive vy value will cause the background layer to move down and a negative vy value will cause it to move up.
steps.instructions:
Code the background layers to move across the screen!


Open Scroller and drag [scroll background with vx (-50) vy (-50)] underneath // scrolling background speed. Notice how the code block turns into JavaScript text:

scroller.scrollBackgroundWithSpeed(-50, -50)


The scrollBackgroundWithSpeed function takes 3 parameters: vx, vy, and layer. After the vy argument, type a comma followed by scroller and a dot operator. Select BackgroundLayer from the code completion tool, then type another dot operator and select Layer1.


Tinker with the vx and vy parameters so that the cloud image scrolls left across the screen. 


Click ▶ to see the cloud image at Layer1 move horizontally across the screen!

steps.hints: ❓Did you use 2 additional setLayerImage functions, and use different layer parameters for each?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What image is displayed at each background layer?

❓ Where will the city and birds background images appear on screen?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Walk the ninja through each background image and its corresponding background layer. Point out to the ninja that the images are ordered from back to front on screen. The images will appear in order from sky, clouds, city, to birds. Explain that the images should be layered in the order they’d like them to appear on screen.
steps.instructions:
Add additional background layers to the project!


Open Scroller and drag another [set image for (layer) to (image)] under // scrolling background set up. Update the layer and image parameters so that the city image variable is set to Layer2.


Repeat this step to add the birds image variable as Layer3 of the background.


Click ▶ to see the city and bird images layered on top of the sky and cloud images.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use 2 additional scrollBackgroundWithSpeed functions, and use different vx parameters so the layers move at different speeds?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What values will cause the background layer to move faster or slower? 

❓ What values will cause the background layer to scroll right? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that a positive vx value will cause the background layer to move right and a negative vx value will cause it to move left. A positive vy value will cause the background layer to move down and a negative vy value will cause it to move up. Larger absolute values will increase the speed and smaller absolute values will decrease the speed.
steps.instructions:
Add movement to the city and bird background layers so that they also move across the screen! 


Open Scroller and drag another [scroll background with vx (-50) vy (-50)] underneath // scrolling background speed. Update the vx and layer parameters so that the city image at Layer2 moves at a slower pace than the sky image at Layer1.


Repeat this step and update the parameters so that the birds image at Layer3 moves right across the screen.


Click ▶ to see the completed project with each background layer moving at different speeds and in different directions on screen!

subgroups.title: City Scroller
subgroups.introduction: Create a project that uses the Background Scroll extension to create a background of different layers, which move at different speeds across the screen.

validationItems.text: Set the sky to background layer 0 and clouds to background layer 1.
Set the city to background layer 2 and birds to background layer 3.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 6 of Purple Belt! Before you create your final Purple Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 6:

badges.title: Extension Explorer
badges.description: Use animation and music code, plus the scroller and story extensions, to enhance a project.

badges.title: Stop Motion
badges.description: Use an array of images to create an animation for a sprite.

badges.title: Path of Least Resistance
badges.description: Use an animation preset path to animate a sprite’s movement.

badges.title: Earworm
badges.description: Create a custom melody using a string of note names.

badges.title: Seven Layer Dip
badges.description: Use the Scroller extension to change the background image layers.

badges.title: Parallax Party
badges.description: Use the Scroller extension to move a background layer to create a parallax effect.

badges.title: The Choice is Yours
badges.description: Use the Story extension to present the player with choices.

badges.title: Stage Directions
badges.description: Use the Story extension to move a sprite to a specific position.

badges.title: What’s my Line?
badges.description: Use the Story extension to have a sprite say text with custom colors.
